events.description: Tadatoshi compares lance and sword practice and weighs Kojirō against Musashi.
Sado is to bring Musashi if found; Kakubei may bring Kojirō for an interview.
events.destination_label: the unknown whereabouts of Musashi and Kojirō

events.description: Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Kakubei brings Tadatoshi's interview invitation; Kojirō first accepts, then refuses out of pride.
Yogorō ambushes the sleeping Kojirō; the chapter closes before the duel's outcome is stated.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Yogorō's corpse is discovered and Kojirō supplies funeral money.
In the interview bout Kojirō breaks Gorōji's real lance and severely injures his pelvis and thigh.
Kojirō repeatedly visits the injured Gorōji, strengthening his position among the retainers.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Kojirō kills two samurai attacking Matahachi and publicly assumes responsibility.
After hearing Matahachi's story, Kojirō follows him and discovers Akemi living with him.
Umpei, an experienced well-digger boss working for the shōgun's castle project, again offers Matahachi higher-paid work inside the castle grounds.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Musashi and Iori build a cabin and Musashi trains the boy's gaze.
Shinzō reports Yogorō's death and invites Musashi to Ujikatsu's residence; they ride away together.
Shinzō reports that Kagenori has died and that Yogorō also died after going alone to seek revenge on Kojirō.
With Yogorō dead, Shinzō says adoption proceedings arranged through his father and Munenori will make him Kagenori's heir and successor to the Obata name.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Musashi detects and circumvents the staged garden ambush prepared to test him.
The group proposes Musashi as shogunal instructor and discusses marrying him to Otsū; Musashi remains reluctant.

Musashi internally rejects the sword of conquest and mere technical instruction, defining the Way instead as a means to establish order, protect and refine the spirit and ultimately contribute to peace and good government.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Akemi leaves Matahachi.
Daizō pays Matahachi to enter Edo Castle as a well digger and kill Hidetada with a hidden musket.
Daizō retrieves the cached advance and finds twenty-eight of thirty gold pieces remaining.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Toranosuke's group abducts Osugi to lure Kojirō.
Kojirō follows news of Osugi’s kidnapping from Takanawa via Yajibei’s house and Kanda toward the Ono residence at Saikachi Slope.
Tadaaki first concedes defeat as a fighter. Kojirō nevertheless attacks and cuts his topknot while Tadaaki cuts Kojirō’s sleeve. Tadaaki accepts responsibility for his students later.
After accepting responsibility, Tadaaki announces retirement, expels Toranosuke, orders the students to train elsewhere and releases Osugi. Later public talk of madness is not a medical fact.
Not many days after the confrontation, Tadaaki leaves Edo for an unstated destination.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
A typhoon destroys the cabin; Musashi helps neighboring farmers before departing with Iori.
After an overnight stop at Tanashi, they are delayed at the Iruma River; Iori finds and buries old battle bones.

Pressed by Iori's questions about loyal and rebel dead, Musashi concludes that a genuine samurai and swordsman must possess compassion and an appreciation of life's poignancy, not merely destructive skill.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Musashi searches donor records for Daizō without finding him.
Watching a drummer use two sticks gives Musashi a new formulation of his two-sword principle.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Baiken's group ambushes Musashi; Musashi kills five and Gonnosuke kills seven with his staff, leaving one lancer-priest survivor.
When Musashi reports the attack, officials bind him as the suspected shrine-treasure thief.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Oko attacks Gonnosuke and he kills her with her own dagger.
Iori follows Daizō and Jōtarō and witnesses the transfer and caching of Mitsumine's stolen treasure.
Takuan sends Tanzaemon toward Shōjuan before finding the unconscious boys; father and son narrowly miss one another.
Iori follows Jōtarō, denounces him as a thief and eventually fights him near the Musashino cabin, using Musashi's eye-training lesson.
The boys discover that both regard Musashi as their teacher; their hostility gives way to shocked recognition even though mistrust remains.
Still struggling in a tree, Iori and Jōtarō fall together and are knocked unconscious.
Jōtarō admits helping Daizō rob the treasure house while claiming the theft serves the public; Takuan attacks the logic of a half-educated do-gooder imposing his own idea of social good.
Jōtarō explains Daizō's plot; Takuan tells him to reunite with his father and flee in disguise.
Gonnosuke and Iori escape the pursuing villagers and shake off the last searchers at Shōmaru Pass.
After Jōtarō's confession, Takuan directs him to seek his father at Shōjuan and flee in disguise.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Osugi arrives to slander Musashi and his recommendation; Iori pelts her with a pomegranate and manure.
Osugi appears at the mansion and gives Shinzō a long denunciation of Musashi, citing Sekigahara, alleged crimes and the Otsū dispute to argue he is unfit to teach the shōgun.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Matahachi abandons the assassination, tries to remove the undelivered musket, escapes confinement and is caught digging by Takuan.
Takuan reveals that Daizō is Mizoguchi Shinano and shaves Matahachi's head.

A retainer reports that Musashi has already been released on Lord Sakai’s instructions after the shrine-treasure misunderstanding was cleared, and handed over to Gonnosuke. This is separate from Hidetada’s later judgment.

After Musashi’s separate release has been reported, Hidetada accepts Takuan’s counsel for constructive government, approves lenient penalties for the conspiracy and looks favorably on Musashi as a tutor.
Matahachi and Akemi are lashed and banished from Edo rather than executed; both remain alive after punishment.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Iori meets the Hosokawa advance party; Kojirō writes a life-and-death challenge for him to carry to Musashi.
Iori finds Musashi and Gonnosuke, delivers the challenge, and returns with them to the cabin.
Next morning Iori rides to return the borrowed horse to the Hōjō household.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Shinzō brings the official summons to Musashi and Gonnosuke at the cabin; Iori is at the Hōjō household.
Musashi travels from the Hōjō household at Ushigome to Wadakura in response to the summons; the previous evening’s cabin-to-Hōjō journey is separate.
Sakai tells Musashi the appointment has been canceled after a sudden change and adverse reports; Musashi expresses relief.
At Sakai's request Musashi paints a Musashino sunrise as a wordless statement of his character.
After finishing the painting, Musashi leaves the pavilion for an unstated destination.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Musashi chooses further wandering, entrusts Iori and the father's pouch to Gonnosuke, and leaves a letter for Hōjō.
Takuan decodes the pouch's clue: Iori's abandoned sister is linked to the single sound of Otsū's flute.
The group hurries to the cabin but finds Musashi already gone.
Musashi leaves the cabin alone for an unspecified mountain journey.

Musashi says the Way of the Sword and good government should ultimately align, but he now sees that governance requires a perfect blending of military and literary arts and that he still has much to learn from the country itself.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
